title: Physics-guided machine learning links Southern Ocean regime shifts to a northward-shifting Antarctic Circumpolar Current
summary: Applying THOR to one eddy-permitting CM4 climate simulation, researchers detected a projected dynamical-regime shift where the Antarctic Circumpolar Current crosses the Pacific–Antarctic Ridge under the SSP5-8.5 scenario. Neural-network explanations and transport analysis attributed the modeled change to stronger wind stress shifting the current northward into less topographically constrained waters, where the flow intensifies. This is a model-based scenario result, not an observed future change.
ai_technology: THOR (Tracking global Heating with Ocean Regimes), using NEMI clustering, an ensemble of 50 multilayer perceptrons, SHAP and layer-wise relevance propagation
organization: University of California, Davis; NOAA Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Laboratory; European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts; Institut Pierre-Simon Laplace

evidence.tested: Applying THOR to one eddy-permitting CM4 climate simulation, researchers detected a projected dynamical-regime shift where the Antarctic Circumpolar Current crosses the Pacific–Antarctic Ridge under the SSP5-8.5 scenario.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint and computational climate-model analysis using CM4/MOM6, one model and the SSP5-8.5 scenario. The paper reports neural-network validation accuracy around 65–70%; it describes the model output and projected shift, not an observed real-world regime transition.
evidence.ai_role: The clustering and neural-network ensemble identified and tracked local ocean dynamical regimes across model scenarios; SHAP and layer-wise relevance propagation highlighted wind-stress curl and bathymetry for follow-up physical analysis.
